title_en: Beautiful Places in China (2/20): Guilin, Dawn on the Li River
note_en: The 把 construction moves the object in front of the verb when something happens to it with a result or destination: 把两岸的青山清清楚楚地倒映在水中 "reflects the green hills on both banks clearly in the water." English simply puts the object after the verb, but in Chinese, when the verb is followed by a place phrase like 在水中, the object usually has to be pulled forward with 把.
